newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich links Reno to Watergate's John Mitchell.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich links Reno to Watergate's John Mitchell.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich Tuesday likened Attorney General Janet Reno to John Mitchell, the attorney general under President Richard Nixon who was jailed on charges related to the Watergate affair.

In a conference call with reporters, Gingrich said he was very disappointed with Reno's decision Monday rejecting an independent probe into alleged improper fund raising by the Democratic Party and President Clinton's White House.
Gingrich said Representative Henry Hyde, an Illinois Republican who heads the House Judiciary Committee, would be looking into the Reno's handling of the matter.
"This was something you might have expected from John Mitchell in 1973 but it's very sad to see Janet Reno doing it in 1997," Gingrich said.

Mitchell, who served as attorney general and manager of Nixon's 1972 re-election campaign, was implicated in the White House cover-up of the Watergate affair that eventually led to Nixon's resignation.

In New York, Clinton was asked about Gingrich's comments and defended Reno, saying: "She had to make a legal decision on a legal matter." He added that, "It should not be a political matter. It should be a legal matter. That's where everybody should leave it."

In letters to Republicans on the House and Senate Judiciary committees, Reno said a Watergate-style special counsel was not justified to investigate Democratic fund-raising activities in the 1996 presidential campaign.

"I was very disappointed last night when the attorney general took that position," Gingrich said. "The facts are overwhelming. The fact is that we have evidence of illegality in foreign contributions ... it's clear the law was broken."
"I think Chairman Hyde will be looking into it," Gingrich added.
Other Republicans in Congress also responded angrily to Reno's decision and some demanded that Reno appear before Congress to justify it.

"I have little choice but to conclude that, much to my disappointment, Attorney General Reno did not receive our request with a mind fully open to doing what is plainly in our nation's best interest," said Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Orrin Hatch, a Utah Republican.
But Democratic Sen. Dick Durbin of Illinois defended Reno. "She calls them like she sees them. I hope Attorney General Reno does not bow to pressure," he told Hatch.
